sentences.text: Lactobacillus iners, first described in 1999, is a prevalent species of the vaginal microbiome that does not grow easily on MRS agar but grows anaerobically on blood agar.
It is reported as the most prevalent vaginal microbe globally, the most fastidious of the vaginal lactobacilli, and the one with the smallest genome.
It makes less lactic acid, only the L-isoform, and uniquely encodes the cholesterol-dependent cytolysin inerolysin, which has led to it being called a pathobiont.
Systematic reviews and meta-analyses have compared L. iners-dominated with L. crispatus-dominated microbiota for bacterial vaginosis and several sexually transmitted infections.
A review of pregnancy describes its frequent presence at all stages of gestation and conflicting data on preterm birth and in vitro fertilisation.
